evidence.finding: Enterprise custom airgap deployments run all Factory inside the customer network. The full local harness skips sign-in, sync, Factory telemetry and crash reporting. It uses configured model endpoints and an optional customer collector, with cloud features unavailable.

evidence.title: Factory individual plans

evidence.locator: Supported editors; VS Code, Cursor, and Windsurf; JetBrains IDEs; Zed; Troubleshooting
evidence.finding: VS Code, Cursor and Windsurf get a Marketplace extension that gives Droid the active file, selection, open files, diagnostics and IDE-native diffs. JetBrains IDEs 2025.3+ run Droid through ACP in AI Chat, which does not yet share open files, selections, diagnostics or diffs. evidence.finding: droid --resume reopens a session, --fork copies a session into a new one, droid exec -s resumes in exec mode, droid loop creates, pauses, resumes or cancels recurring prompts, and /share shares a session with the organization.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Factory App

evidence.finding: The Factory App runs on macOS, Windows and Linux. Documents, spreadsheets, PDFs, live websites and code diffs render beside the session; design mode and inline diff comments send feedback to Droid. Local, web and mobile review surfaces connect to the same Factory runtime; sessions are filtered and grouped across projects and machines. It describes sessions and workstreams, not an issue tracker.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Individual Plans
evidence.locator: Individual plan tiers; How individual usage works; Missions; FAQ
evidence.finding: Free uses your own inference (ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot or OpenRouter sign-in, or your own keys); Pro, Plus and Max use Factory Managed Inference under 5-hour, 7-day and 30-day rolling rate limits. Sessions consume Factory Standard Credits by model plus compute usage for cloud environments. Droid Core is a free open-weight pool with separate limits; Extra Usage is prepaid USD credit, $10 minimum, no expiry, drawn as sessions use models. evidence.title: Factory docs: Organization Plans
evidence.locator: Business; Enterprise; What organization plans add; Usage and billing
evidence.finding: Teams has up to 10 seats, each with Pro rate limits, billed centrally month-to-month. Business adds custom limits, SSO, SAML/SCIM, ZDR, audit logs and basic admin controls; Enterprise adds unlimited seats, dedicated compute, on-premise options, sub-organizations, data residency and priority support with SLAs. Business and Enterprise are contract-priced through sales.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Contact Support
evidence.finding: Support channels are email (support@factory.com), Discord and public GitHub issues; no response times are published on the page.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Feature Maturity
evidence.finding: Features still maturing carry a Private Preview or deprecation tag; untagged features are generally available. The CLI is versioned and the app ships continuously.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Workstreams
evidence.locator: Beta note; How a workstream is organized; When to use; How it works
evidence.finding: Workstreams are beta on Pro, Plus, Max and Teams, not yet Business or Enterprise. An orchestrator splits a goal across Droid agent sessions that report progress, blockers and finished work; work comes back as PRs. A workstream keeps going as work is added and targets days-to-weeks projects; regular sessions are for one-off work. Agents are Droid sessions using the machine's models, skills, MCP, hooks and AGENTS.md.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Steer a Workstream
evidence.locator: What the orchestrator does; Talk to the orchestrator; Follow agents; /migrate
evidence.finding: Users message the orchestrator any time to add work, change direction or set rules; agents report blockers to it in messages. The Agents tab groups agents as Waiting on you (questions or tool approvals), Working and Idle, with latest activity and PRs. Users can open an agent, approve or deny tool calls, message it or stop its turn. /migrate agrees outcome, scope and validation, asks for plan approval and hands over evidence.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Workstream Settings and Usage
evidence.locator: Workstream settings; Usage; Usage limits; Organization controls
evidence.finding: Each workstream sets orchestrator and agent models and reasoning effort; models can be changed while agents work. The Usage section shows credits used, agent count and per-session credits. Workstreams have no separate fee and stop at usage limits; BYOK models can be used.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Workstream Machines
evidence.locator: Machine types; Choose the orchestrator machine; Choose where agents run
evidence.finding: Orchestrator and agents run on fresh environment computers, Droid Computers (Factory-managed or your own via Remote Control) or Local. Agents on environment or managed computers keep working after the laptop closes; Remote Control machines must be online; Local stops when the app quits. Local agents share the chosen working directory unless a worktree is selected.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Workstream Tasks
evidence.locator: Private Preview note; Statuses; Open a task; Act on a task; After you send an action; Troubleshooting
evidence.finding: The Tasks tab (CVE remediation, Private Preview) lists one fix per task with statuses; fix droids watch CI and fix it up to three rounds before Fix failed. Overview shows severity, package, plan and PR; plans state how to roll back. Actions include Approve plan, Request changes, Merge PR and Retry; the bar shows the main action and offers the next waiting task. Factory does not enforce plan or merge approval and advises branch protection. Each action carries the task version so it is not applied twice, and a changed task returns Not applied. A fix droid that stops responding is not detected automatically.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Workstream Pull Requests
evidence.finding: The PRs tab lists PRs agents opened or worked on with checks and review counts; a PR tab has Conversation, Diff, Walkthrough and Validation views plus Review and Merge buttons.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Workstream Automations
evidence.locator: Create an automation; Where runs go and where they run; The Automations tab
evidence.finding: Users ask the orchestrator in plain words to create recurring automations; runs deliver to the creating session. Cloud machines keep running after the laptop closes, Remote Control machines must be online and Local needs the desktop app running.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Custom automations
evidence.locator: Triggers; Where it runs (computer limits, session privacy); Memory & Evolution; Webhook triggers; Review deliveries; Run health and alerts; Automatic pauses
evidence.finding: Automations start Droid sessions on a schedule, a Slack message, a GitHub event or an inbound webhook POST (secret header); no outbound event webhooks are described. Scheduled and Slack runs execute on the desktop-app machine or a Droid Computer, webhook runs on a Droid Computer or Environment. Factory-managed computers host up to 10 automations (5 per minute). Session privacy is Private or Team. Scheduled automations have optional Memory & Evolution. Webhook deliveries are kept 30 days in an Events feed; identical bodies within 10 minutes are Deduped, deliveries beyond the hourly limit (10 by default, 1-60) are Rate-capped, and a delivery is Skipped when paused, a previous run is in progress or the computer is over capacity. Status Degraded means the first or a retried run failed; five failed scheduled runs in a row, 10 days of missed runs on your own machine, or an over-capacity computer pause the automation, with the reason in Events and alert emails. A run that stops reporting progress is marked failed.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Droid Computers
evidence.locator: Introduction; Provisioning; Persistent compute pools (size the pool, how Factory uses the pool); Port forwarding; Resource metrics and statuses; Git credentials; Security (firewall)
evidence.finding: Droid Computers are Factory-managed persistent computers that keep packages, files, running services and configuration between sessions; they auto-pause when idle and can set up dependencies on creation. Delegation pools run up to a per-machine parallel worker limit (default 3, 1-50); a session holds its slot while running and 30 minutes after going idle; when every computer is full, requests wait for a slot. droid computer port-forward forwards local TCP ports over the relay. Detail pages show CPU, memory and disk metrics and statuses including Error. GitHub App credentials are added automatically. iptables allow only the daemon port inbound, but factory-user has passwordless sudo and could change the rules. The page no longer states machine size.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Droid Computers API
evidence.locator: Retry the install-dependencies step (POST /api/v0/computers/{computerId}/install-deps); Get computer metrics
evidence.finding: The Computers API can retry the install-dependencies step and returns computer metrics.

Image and PDF attachments and PDF previews are supported. Latest entry: CLI and Desktop v1.16.0, 2026-11-20.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Environment prerequisites
evidence.locator: Check access and compute policy; Connect source control; Configure runtime secrets
evidence.finding: Factory-hosted Environments need an active paid subscription and an allowed compute policy; free accounts cannot launch them, and trial, ended or overdue states can block managed compute; Factory-hosted compute is unavailable for EU-region organizations. GitHub, GitLab and configured self-hosted source control are supported. Managed-computer secrets from Settings > Account > Secrets become environment variables at runtime.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Environments
evidence.finding: An Environment is a saved setup (source, repositories, setup commands) that Factory builds into a reusable snapshot; each instance starts from it, and instance changes do not alter the Environment.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Run Droids on an Environment
evidence.locator: Start a session; Run multiple Droids in parallel
evidence.finding: Each launch from an Environment creates its own instance with provisioning progress shown, so parallel agents do not share working-tree changes; parallel launches depend on organization compute limits, provider capacity and usage allowances. The virtualization type is not stated.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Linear delegation
evidence.locator: Prerequisites; Delegate an issue; Follow progress and review results; Stop a running task
evidence.finding: Linear issues are delegated by assigning Factory or mentioning @Factory; Droid receives the title, description, labels and comments and runs on a remote computer as the organization's Agent Profile. A paid plan is required. Factory posts progress and results, attaches PR links from the final response and moves a backlog or to-do issue into a started state; other issue edits stay in Linear. Stop halts the run and does not undo work already done; the session stays open for review.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Delegations
evidence.locator: Introduction; Prerequisites; Personal and shared identity; Repository access for the Agent Profile; Set personal delegation defaults
evidence.finding: Work is delegated from Slack, Linear, Jira, Microsoft Teams and Google Chat. Shared channel and issue requests run as an Agent Profile with its own Git credentials and connectors; direct messages run as the sender. Factory matches the requester by the same account email in both apps. Personal delegation instructions apply to follow-up messages in those sessions. Factory is not described as owning a tracker; issues stay in the connected app.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Analytics API
evidence.locator: Introduction and permissions; Endpoints; Sessions; Factory Standard Credits usage; Pull requests; Tickets; Projects
evidence.finding: The Analytics API reports Factory Standard Credits usage, tool usage, activity and productivity in daily UTC rows (the current day is partial). In Private Preview, /sessions returns one row per root session with sub-agents folded in, and /prs, /tickets and /projects attribute credits per pull request, Linear or Jira issue, and Linear project or Jira epic. Organization routes need Enterprise and a Manager or Owner; some need a preview allowlist.

evidence.title: Factory docs: API reference
evidence.finding: The Factory Public API authenticates with a bearer Factory API key or JWT; service accounts have their own API keys. API version 0.1.0; no deprecation policy is stated on the page.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Sessions API
evidence.locator: List, create, get, delete, update sessions; list child sessions; pending elicitations; interrupt; messages
evidence.finding: The Sessions API lists, creates, gets, updates and deletes sessions, lists child sessions, answers pending elicitations, interrupts a session and reads or adds messages.

evidence.title: Factory docs: TypeScript SDK
evidence.finding: @factory/droid-sdk starts Droid as a subprocess, connects to a daemon or calls the REST API, with persistent sessions and in-process MCP tools defined with tool() and createSdkMcpServer.

evidence.title: Factory-AI public GitHub repositories
evidence.locator: GitHub organization repository list and licenses; Factory-AI/factory contents; npm registry metadata for droid and @factory/droid-sdk
evidence.finding: Public repositories include droid-sdk-python (Apache-2.0, main a4103054...) and droid-sdk-typescript (LICENSE file Apache-2.0), droid-code-review and skills (MIT) and factory-zed-extension (Apache-2.0). Factory-AI/factory holds docs and issues with no license file. The droid CLI npm package is UNLICENSED; its latest version is 1.17.1, published 2026-11-21. @factory/droid-sdk 0.11.0 is Apache-2.0.

evidence.finding: Open user report (2026-11-05): Workstream settings model pickers do not offer locally configured BYOK custom models, and SpawnAgent has no model or reasoning parameters; the reporter could not tell whether this is intended.

evidence.title: Factory docs: BYOK
evidence.locator: Introduction; Configure custom models; provider field
evidence.finding: BYOK custom models use OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock or generic chat-completions-compatible endpoints, including local models. Keys stay local in settings.json; personal custom models appear in the CLI and desktop app but not on Factory's hosted web or mobile surfaces. There is no adapter for other agent harnesses.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Available Models
evidence.finding: Factory-hosted models come from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI and the Droid Core open-model pool, each with a credit multiplier; all run in the Droid harness.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Missions reference
evidence.finding: Missions set separate models and reasoning effort for the orchestrator, workers and validators.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Factory Missions
evidence.locator: Introduction; When to use; Collaborative Planning
evidence.finding: Missions plan features, milestones and success criteria with Droid before any code is written and validate progress. The docs say not to run a long normal session and then convert it into a Mission; start a new Mission instead.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Droid CLI
evidence.finding: The Droid CLI is the terminal surface for the same platform, extended with MCP, hooks, skills and custom droids; no third-party agent harness is offered.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Droid Exec
evidence.finding: droid exec runs Droid non-interactively for scripts and CI.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Autonomy Level
evidence.locator: Levels table; How it works; Command allowlists; Where Autonomy Level applies
evidence.finding: Autonomy Off, Low, Medium or High sets the highest-risk command or MCP tool that runs without approval; higher-risk calls ask first. Permission rules allow, ask (even at High) or block (no approval path) commands. Choosing allow always raises the session's level; sandbox allow-always persists the path or domain. droid exec is read-only by default; new sessions start at the user's default level, capped by organization policy. Spec Mode is read-only planning.

evidence.title: Factory docs: OS-level sandbox
evidence.locator: Introduction; Isolation scope (per-command, whole-process); Enable and configure; Default access policies
evidence.finding: An opt-in sandbox (sandbox.enabled) confines Droid-initiated commands with Seatbelt on macOS or bubblewrap plus seccomp on Linux, kernel-enforced. Default policy allows reads except denyRead, denies writes outside the working directory, and routes network through a proxy that allows only Factory and WorkOS domains plus listed domains. Modes: per-command (default) or whole-process; it blocks rather than running unisolated. Settings resolve org > project > user.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Interaction Modes
evidence.finding: Spec Mode uses read-only planning and asks for approval before implementation.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Enterprise Controls & Managed Settings
evidence.locator: The settings levels; precedence; maxAutonomyLevel; mcpPolicy; mcpAutonomyOverrides; permission rules
evidence.finding: Settings levels are Org, Folder, Project and User; for hard controls Org wins. Organizations set maxAutonomyLevel, permission rules, sandbox, managed hooks, model policy and an MCP allowlist (mcpPolicy) with per-server and per-tool autonomy overrides (mcpAutonomyOverrides).

evidence.title: Factory docs: Droid Shield
evidence.finding: Droid Shield scans added lines before Droid runs git commit or git push and blocks the operation if it detects secrets. To proceed the user commits manually or disables Droid Shield in settings; manual git outside Droid is not scanned.

evidence.title: Factory docs: MCP
evidence.locator: Quick start (registry); droid mcp add; remote OAuth
evidence.finding: Droid is an MCP client for stdio, http and sse servers, with a built-in registry, /mcp manager, droid mcp add and browser OAuth for remote servers. The page documents no Factory MCP server for other agents.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Connectors
evidence.finding: Connectors give Droid Factory-managed access to apps such as Linear, Jira, Notion, Slack, Sentry and Google Workspace; connections belong to the Factory user and organization, and some apps use an organization-registered OAuth app.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Plugins
evidence.finding: Plugins bundle skills, slash commands, droids, output styles, hooks and MCP servers; organizations can run internal marketplaces.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Skills
evidence.finding: Skills are SKILL.md folders; team-shared skills live under .factory/skills/ in the repository, personal skills in user directories.

evidence.title: Factory docs: AGENTS.md
evidence.locator: Create one root file; instruction sources table
evidence.finding: A root AGENTS.md, with nested files where needed, is loaded as coding guidelines at startup and during dynamic discovery.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Hooks
evidence.finding: Hooks run shell commands at lifecycle events such as PreToolUse for validation, policy and automation.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Telemetry privacy
evidence.locator: What reaches Factory versus your collector; granularity
evidence.finding: Droid sends OpenTelemetry metrics to Factory by default (never in airgapped deployments); spans with message content go only to a customer collector and content only on opt-in. Granularity user (default) carries per-user identity; aggregate strips identities.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Privacy and data flows
evidence.finding: Telemetry is OpenTelemetry metrics by default with optional content spans to a customer collector.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Security
evidence.finding: OAuth login with encrypted token storage that auto-rotates every 30 days. Droid reads and edits files where it runs and does not require uploading or indexing a static copy of the repository.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Compliance, audit and monitoring
evidence.finding: The Trust Center at trust.factory.com holds reports, security architecture documents and sub-processor lists. On 2026-11-21 trust.factory.com rendered only its title to a plain fetch, and factory.com/security returned a Cloudflare 403.

evidence.title: Factory docs: AutoWiki
evidence.finding: AutoWiki generates browsable wikis for repositories; /install-wiki sets up refresh on every push.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Factory App Quickstart
evidence.finding: Download and install the app, sign in, set a working directory, select a model and send a first prompt.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Remote Control

evidence.finding: Install the CLI, sign in, and run droid daemon --remote-control; the computer connects outbound through Factory's relay with no inbound ports. Keeping the daemon running across reboots is not described.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Worktrees
evidence.locator: What a worktree is; Start a session in a worktree
evidence.finding: The app creates a separate Git worktree for a session from a chosen base branch, creating a new branch by default, or uses an existing branch.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Droid Control
evidence.finding: Droid Control operates terminals, browsers and desktop apps, reports QA flows with annotated screenshots and records before/after comparison videos of PRs.

evidence.title: Factory docs: Automated code review
evidence.finding: Automated review on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps posts a summary and inline comments on pull requests.

evidence.title: Factory docs: OpenCompute

routing.answer: The orchestrator splits the goal into areas and starts the corresponding workers.

messages.answer: The orchestrator asks agents for updates and sends additional work.

results_return.answer: Agents report completion, blockers and changed assumptions to the orchestrator.

live_progress.answer: Agents are grouped by Waiting on you, Working or Idle with latest activity.

followup.answer: The orchestrator reuses agents for related work.

invocation.answer: /migrate starts a bounded job after human plan approval.

stop.answer: The UI stops an individual agent turn.

steer.answer: Humans can message the orchestrator or agent during active work.

pending_decisions.answer: The Agents tab groups agents awaiting a human question or tool approval.

parent_child.answer: Agents are separate Droid sessions reporting to one workstream orchestrator.

attention.answer: The Agents tab groups sessions waiting on the user.

history.answer: Opening an agent reveals its conversation, tools and changes.

branch.answer: A new worktree creates its own branch from a selected base by default.

worktree.answer: Factory-managed worktrees isolate each session checkout on local machines or connected Droid Computers.

expiry.answer: Persistent worktrees never clean up automatically; ephemeral worktrees are eligible unless a session is pinned.

enforcement.answer: The usage guide explicitly says agents stop once their applicable usage limit is reached.

session_cost.answer: Workstream Usage lists each session credit consumption and its share of total.

child_cost.answer: The workstream breakdown includes agent sessions.

epic_cost.answer: A workstream shows its total credits.

alerts.answer: A banner appears at 90% of the usage allowance.

drilldown.answer: Usage breaks down credits by session and model.

host_awareness.answer: Workstream defaults describe additional machines for orchestrator routing.

shared_limits.answer: Workstream agents share the normal Factory allowance and organization limits.

organization_roles.answer: Owner, Manager and User have distinct organization permissions.

provisioning.answer: SSO and directory synchronization map IdP groups to Factory roles.

revocation.answer: Directory membership changes propagate to Factory; end-to-end immediate session revocation was not tested.

actions.answer: Enterprise owners can inspect organization administrative events.

edits.answer: Managed settings updates have revision-tracked before/after differences.

cross_user_persistence.answer: Audit events identify the acting human or service principal.

pending_reviews.answer: The PRs tab lists each workstream PR with its checks and review activity.

change_understanding.answer: PR tabs offer Diff, Walkthrough and Validation views.

comments.answer: The Conversation view shows PR description and comments.

documents.answer: Workstream shared files retain plans, notes, findings and reports.

gallery.answer: Files supports list/grid, folder browsing, search and type filters.

task_links.answer: A linked shared file opens in the workstream Files tab.

persistence.answer: Shared documents sync across machines and reappear when disabled shared folders are reenabled.

child_findings.answer: Workers save their findings in the orchestrator-designated shared folder.

independent_review.answer: Validation workers check each mission milestone.

spec_checks.answer: Milestone validation tests agreed work; requirement conflict detection and immutable approval gates remain unestablished.

configured_policy.answer: Mission settings can disable QA validation.

pull_requests.answer: Workstreams track PRs opened or worked on by the orchestrator and agents.

comments.answer: PR tabs show comments and review threads.

next_actions.answer: GitHub rows offer open-for-review, draft, close and reopen actions.

export.answer: Humans can download shared-folder documents or copy their contents.

import.answer: Humans upload files or folders as workstream references.

account_independence.answer: Airgap Mode skips sign-in and does not require a Factory account.

code_data.answer: Airgap execution and files remain inside the customer network, subject to its infrastructure egress rules.

prompts.answer: Model traffic can go directly to configured enterprise provider APIs or gateways.

logs.answer: The hosted control plane can retain authentication, administrative and operational logs.
